title: Sample: Fractions (test chapter)
bookChapter: Test chapter written by the CTO for app testing; not part of the course

preamble.whatYouWillLearn: How to compare, add and find fractions of amounts.
preamble.whyItMatters: Fractions are everywhere: sharing, cooking and measuring all use them.

subtopics.title: Equivalent fractions
subtopics.summary: Different fractions that show the same amount.

subtopics.title: Adding fractions
subtopics.summary: Adding fractions with the same and different denominators.

subtopics.title: Fractions of amounts
subtopics.summary: Finding a fraction of a number or a quantity.

questions.solution: Multiply the top and bottom of 1/2 by 2: 1/2 = 2/4.

misconceptions.1: 1/4 is half of a half, not a half.
misconceptions.2: Adding 1 to the top and bottom does not keep a fraction the same.
misconceptions.3: 3/5 is more than a half: 3 is more than half of 5.

questions.prompt: Choose ALL the fractions equal to 3/4.
questions.solution: 3/4 = 6/8 = 9/12 = 75/100 (multiply top and bottom by the same number).

misconceptions.2: Doubling only the bottom halves the fraction.
misconceptions.3: Adding 1 to the top and bottom changes the size.

questions.prompt: True or false: 2/3 is equal to 4/6.
questions.solution: Multiply the top and bottom of 2/3 by 2 to get 4/6, so it is true.

misconceptions.common: Fractions with different numbers can still be the same amount.

questions.prompt: Put these fractions in order from smallest to largest.

misconceptions.common: A bigger denominator does not always mean a bigger fraction; compare with a common denominator.

questions.prompt: Work out 1/4 + 2/4. Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: The denominators are the same, so add the tops: 1 + 2 = 3. The answer is 3/4.

misconceptions.3/8: Do not add the denominators: the pieces are still quarters.
misconceptions.common: Add the numerators only when the denominators match.

misconceptions.0: You added the tops and the bottoms. Change to a common denominator first.
misconceptions.2: You changed the denominator but kept the tops the same.
misconceptions.3: That is the difference, not the sum.

questions.prompt: Mia drinks 1 1/2 litres of water on Monday and 3/4 of a litre on Tuesday. How many litres does she drink altogether?

misconceptions.common: Change 1/2 into quarters before adding, then turn 5/4 into 1 1/4.

questions.prompt: What is the name for the bottom number of a fraction?
questions.solution: The bottom number is the denominator. It tells you how many equal parts make a whole.

misconceptions.numerator: The numerator is the top number.

misconceptions.150: You multiplied by 5. To find 1/5, divide by 5.
misconceptions.common: To find one fifth, divide by 5.

questions.prompt: Match each calculation with its answer.

misconceptions.common: Find one part first (divide by the denominator), then multiply by the numerator.

questions.prompt: A shop has 48 apples. It sells 5/8 of them. How many apples are left?
questions.solution: 1/8 of 48 = 6, so 5/8 = 30 apples sold. 48 - 30 = 18 apples are left.

misconceptions.0: 30 is how many were sold. The question asks how many are left.

questions.prompt: To find 2/3 of a number, you divide by 3 and then do what?
questions.solution: Divide by the denominator (3) to find one third, then multiply by the numerator (2).

misconceptions.common: After finding one part, multiply by the numerator.
